I will keep my land mainly in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I am 65, so I will choose the simplest and steadiest way to farm, not something that needs too much hand labor or too much market gambling. In my place, wheat and maize are the crops I know best, the machines are easy to hire, the seed is easy to buy, and the grain is easy to sell. That matters to me more than chasing a higher but uncertain income from vegetables or other cash crops.

I will plant improved winter wheat on all my land first, then after harvest I will plant summer maize on the same land. I would rather use improved seed than old saved seed because I want more stable emergence, more even fields, and less trouble. I will not make the fertilizer too heavy, because I do not want waste or lodging, but I will feed the crop enough to keep yield steady. For wheat, I will irrigate at the key times, mainly around overwintering, jointing, and grain filling if water allows. For maize, I will keep it simpler and water fewer times, mainly around sowing and the big demand stage. I will spray only when I see real weed, disease, or insect pressure, because every spray costs money and effort.

I will manage the land in a practical way. Before wheat I will plough so the soil loosens well and crop residue mixes in better. After wheat harvest, I will move fast into summer maize and use rotary tillage so I can sow on time. I will watch the field often, keep plant stand even, topdress at the main growth stage, and harvest on time. My goal is not the most aggressive yield. My goal is a crop plan I can actually carry through safely, with stable grain output and manageable labor.
